{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mn-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"58288e8f9ed656f623035e475f7d21d6a1ea108ef0285f89bb679690e254be4e","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mn-class-d:lineage:86","source_registry_sha256":"960e2daa314aff60b32f5124e42324d79615ce2a3ea953a336216b4593c0c910","source_liveness_sha256":"0b70283fc58b1f8ea1822994a92e3ce7ff4b722004376a9cd819180969b6fe1e"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Sign confusables and continuation facts","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: sign colors, regulatory versus warning no-passing signs, intersection and road-shape warnings, lane and merge signs, construction signs, service, guide and route signs","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: sign colors, regulatory versus warning no-passing signs, intersection and road-shape warnings, lane and merge signs, construction signs, service, guide and route signs
Confusable pairs among the sign meanings, followed by continuation facts on warning, construction and guide signs; only the printed text meanings are used, each block ties to one manual page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec09-R01 | anchor: A01
Besides colors, the manual names seven common sign shapes: octagon, triangle, diamond, rectangle, pentagon, crossbuck and circle. [A01]
Why it matters: group sign shapes; text list only, the shapes themselves are pictures.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-R02 | anchor: A01
Road signs combine uniform symbols and pictures with written instructions. [A01]
Why it matters: group signs; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-R03 | anchor: A01
Yellow and yellow-green both warn, but yellow-green is limited to pedestrian and bicycle crossings and school areas, while orange is the color of construction zones. [A01]
Why it matters: group sign colors; confusable yellow versus yellow-green versus orange; difficulty high.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-R04 | anchor: A02
A Do Not Enter sign facing you forbids going into that lane or road, while a Wrong Way sign means you are already in a lane of oncoming traffic. [A02]
Why it matters: group regulatory signs; confusable do not enter versus wrong way; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-R05 | anchor: A03
In the multilane roundabout sign example, going straight is allowed from either lane even though turning right and turning left are each limited to one lane. [A03]
Why it matters: group roundabout signs; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec09-R06 | anchor: A05
Located on the left side of a two-way highway, the No Passing Zone warning sign alerts drivers to the start of a no-passing zone [A05].
Why it matters: group no-passing signs; confusable regulatory versus warning version; difficulty high.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-R07 | anchor: A05
The school crossing and pedestrian crossing signs each come with an arrow sign below them, which the manual calls the standard marking. [A05]
Why it matters: group crossing signs; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-R08 | anchor: A06
A crossroad sign means an intersection is ahead and you should prepare to yield. [A06]
Why it matters: group intersection warnings; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-R09 | anchor: A06
A side road sign means traffic is coming from your right, so watch for vehicles entering the road. [A06]
Why it matters: group intersection warnings; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-R10 | anchor: A06
A Y-intersection sign means the road splits in two directions, so expect crossing traffic and get ready to bear one way or the other. [A06]
Why it matters: group intersection warnings; confusable Y versus T; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-R11 | anchor: A07
A roundabout warning sign means slow to the advisory speed as you approach and be ready to stop. [A07]
Why it matters: group road-shape warnings; difficulty low.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-R12 | anchor: A07
A winding road sign means the road bends back and forth ahead, while a road turns ahead sign means it changes direction sharply; slow down for both. [A07]
Why it matters: group road-shape warnings; confusable winding versus sharp turn; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-R13 | anchor: A07
A two-way traffic ahead sign means you are leaving a one-way road for a two-way road, so stay to the right. [A07]
Why it matters: group divided and two-way signs; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-R14 | anchor: A07
A divided highway begins sign tells you to stay right as the road divides, while a divided highway ends sign warns that two-way traffic will no longer be separated by a center island. [A07]
Why it matters: group divided and two-way signs; confusable begins versus ends; difficulty high.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-R15 | anchor: A07
A traffic signal ahead sign warns that the next intersection has a traffic light. [A07]
Why it matters: group warnings; difficulty low.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-R16 | anchor: A08
Crossing signs warn you to watch for animals, people or vehicles crossing the road. [A08]
Why it matters: group crossing warnings; difficulty low.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec09-R17 | anchor: A08
A steep hill sign means the road drops sharply ahead, so be sure your brakes work before you go on. [A08]
Why it matters: group road warnings; difficulty low.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec09-R18 | anchor: A08
With a lane ends sign the ending lane must yield and merge, with a merging traffic sign you make room for vehicles joining your road, and with an added lane sign the new traffic does not need to merge at all. [A08]
Why it matters: group merge signs; confusable lane ends versus merging versus added lane; difficulty high.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec09-R19 | anchor: A08
A narrow bridge sign means the bridge ahead is narrower than the road leading to it. [A08]
Why it matters: group road warnings; difficulty low.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec09-R20 | anchor: A09
A flagger sign means a person with a flag is ahead, so drive cautiously. [A09]
Why it matters: group construction signs; difficulty low.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec09-R21 | anchor: A09
A road work sign showing workers means maintenance is under way, so slow down and shift your lane position to keep away from them. [A09]
Why it matters: group construction signs; difficulty low.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec09-R22 | anchor: A09
Reduced speed limits are often posted in work zones. [A09]
Why it matters: group construction signs; links to the work zone fine.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec09-R23 | anchor: A09
Brown signs point out historic sites, parks and other points of interest. [A09]
Why it matters: group guide signs; confusable brown versus blue versus green.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec09-R24 | anchor: A10
Blue signs lead you to motorist services such as telephones, gas, food, motels, hospitals and rest areas. [A10]
Why it matters: group guide signs; difficulty low.
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec09-R25 | anchor: A10
Green signs show exits, distances to cities, interstate interchanges, street or route names and bicycle routes. [A10]
Why it matters: group guide signs; difficulty low.
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec09-R26 | anchor: A10
Route signs identify the type of road, with separate markers for interstate freeways, U.S. highways, Minnesota highways and county roads. [A10]
Why it matters: group route signs; the marker shapes are pictures and are not described here.
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec09-R27 | anchor: A10
Traffic-control signals are placed at busy intersections to promote safety and orderly traffic flow. [A10]
Why it matters: group signals; prereq for the dark signal rule.
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0068]
